data.source_title: Obstetric triage improvement process using the Donabedian model of quality care: a quality improvement initiative
data.locator: Methods, baseline audit and sample; Results, Figure 1 (arrival-after-registration to initial nursing assessment).
data.source_setting: Labor-and-delivery triage at a tertiary hospital in Pakistan; booked patients >=24 weeks gestation were assessed there, while unbooked or <24-week patients went to the emergency department.
data.source_period: Baseline audit during the first quarter of 2018; post-intervention audit after six PDSA cycles; exact post-audit dates and intervention duration are not consistently reported.
data.source_n: Convenience audit sample n=200 (100 pre, 100 post); facility handled about 400-500 triage visits/month, which is throughput context rather than the audit denominator.
data.quantity: Share meeting a 5-minute arrival-to-initial-nursing-assessment target, pre vs post redesign
data.source_evidence_basis: The paper's pre/post audit reports 6% meeting the 5-minute target before redesign and 65% afterward. The redesign included acuity-based prioritization, assigned triage roles, a two-stage assessment and handoff, staffing/training changes, and recurring audits.
data.limitations: Single-site quality-improvement project in a tertiary Pakistan hospital; small convenience samples and bundled PDSA changes limit causal attribution. The intervention is described as a six-month project, but exact post-audit dates are not provided. Not an RWJ measurement or a clinical triage rule.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Model arrival, brief initial screen, acuity-based queue priority, assessment-room handoff, and onward disposition as distinct states; retain the reported before/after proportions only as external process context, never as RWJ performance targets.

data.source_title: Obstetric triage improvement process using the Donabedian model of quality care: a quality improvement initiative
data.locator: Results, Figure 2 and text on length of stay; endpoint is time in L&D triage, not delivery admission-to-discharge duration.
data.source_setting: Same tertiary-hospital L&D triage service in Pakistan.
data.source_period: Baseline audit during first quarter 2018; post-intervention audit after six PDSA cycles; exact post-audit dates are not reported.
data.source_n: Convenience audit sample n=200 (100 pre, 100 post). Pre-intervention LOS was undocumented for 16% in the initial baseline review; charted LOS ranges are reported for the audited cohort.
data.quantity: Reported L&D-triage length of stay range and post-audit patient shares
data.unit: minutes; post shares are percent of audited patients
data.source_evidence_basis: The paper reports pre-intervention triage LOS from 30 to 240 minutes, with 64% meeting a 120-minute local benchmark; after redesign it reports 75% with 30-minute LOS and 25% with 60-minute LOS.
data.limitations: The endpoint is triage visit duration, not labor, delivery, postpartum stay, or NICU length of stay. Small single-center convenience sample; baseline LOS was missing for some records and intervention package is bundled. The paper's narrative also summarizes LOS as 240 to 60 minutes, so retain the detailed reported range and shares rather than infer a common mean or distribution.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Keep triage LOS distinct from the subsequent labor-and-delivery and postpartum unit stays; use as a workflow segmentation clue and external observed range only, not a fitted service-time distribution.

data.source_title: Obstetric triage improvement process using the Donabedian model of quality care: a quality improvement initiative
data.locator: Methods, Problem and PDSA cycles; Results, post-implementation acuity distribution; process diagram and sixth PDSA cycle.
data.source_setting: Same tertiary Pakistan hospital; 24/7 triage for pregnancy concerns, labor and birth, medical complaints, and maternal-fetal surveillance.
data.source_period: Project initiated after a 2018 sentinel event; baseline audit first quarter 2018; six PDSA cycles; post-audit calendar window not specified.
data.source_n: Service context: >6,000 deliveries/year and 400-500 L&D triage visits/month. Post-implementation acuity distribution denominator is the 100-patient post-audit sample.
data.quantity: Documented post-redesign triage acuity categories and specified process sequence

workflow: direct labor-room or operating-theatre transfer for level-1 cases

data.unit: percent of post-audit patients; qualitative workflow sequence
data.source_evidence_basis: After implementation, the audit categorized 3% red, 5% amber, 77% green, and 15% white/non-urgent. The paper specifies an assigned triage nurse, brief first assessment, documentation, handoff to a second nurse, further assessment, and direct transfer to labor room or operating theatre for the highest urgency category.
data.limitations: This is a report of one hospital's locally adapted process and audit mix; category shares are not general prevalence estimates. Acuity labels and routing thresholds are institutional clinical content and must not be copied as treatment rules. Exact post-audit dates are absent.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Use only as a candidate maternity pathway structure: triage can discharge, continue evaluation, admit to labor-and-delivery, or route to a procedural area; model separate staff roles and handoff events. Require local clinical governance for all decision rules.
